html:
The 19th men's football World Cup, held in South Africa from 11 June to 11 July 2010, the first on African soil.

FIFA had opened the bidding only to African countries, and in 2004 chose South Africa over Egypt and Morocco. Sixteen years after the end of apartheid, the country used the tournament to show itself to the world. Ten stadiums in nine cities were built or rebuilt, and the opening match and the final were played at Soccer City in Johannesburg.

Thirty-two teams took part. The drone of the plastic vuvuzela horn became the sound of the tournament. South Africa became the first host to go out in the first round. Ghana came closest of the African teams, losing its quarter final to Uruguay on penalties. Nelson Mandela, aged 91, appeared briefly before the final, his last major public appearance. Spain beat the Netherlands 1 to 0 after extra time for its first title. The cup had come a long way from the first World Cup in Uruguay in 1930.
sum: The 19th men's football World Cup, held in South Africa from 11 June to 11 July 2010, the first on African soil.
